p.n: The Cat Calls Back the Rat

body.p:
the rat wanted to come out of the burrow, but he saw
the cat and did not come close to him. ‘Why don’t you approach me, O gracious

p.n: The Cat Reminds the Rat of their Friendship

body.p: ‘I would love to reward you for your beneficence and let you taste the fruits of your deed.

Approach me and fear not: you are dearer to me than myself,’ and he swore he did not want to do him harm.
”

p.n: The Treatment of Friends or Foes

body.p: ‘He who fails to appease friends and enemies,’ said the rat, ‘harms and ruins himself.

p.n: One Should Not Befriend an Enemy Indefinitely

body.p:
Enmity and friendship are of such a nature that the wise man acts
according to their nature . . . should not fraternize with someone unto whom he was an enemy,
except in the case of necessity.

p.n: Young Cattle Only Nurse for a While

body.p:
